The scanner detects 18 out of 20 infected devices. That means it correctly identifies 18 as infected. But there are 20 infected devices in total, so those 18 are true positives. Then, the scanner also flags 16 uninfected devices. Those would be false positives.

So, total flagged devices are the true positives plus the false positives. That's 18 + 16 = 34 devices. Now, out of these 34 flagged devices, how many are actually infected? Well, the 18 that were correctly detected. So the probability would be 18 divided by 34. Let me simplify that fraction. 18/34 can be reduced by dividing numerator and denominator by 2, which gives 9/17.
